name: stri_sub_replace_all
title: Replace multiple substrings and return the copy

origin.description: Replace several substrings in each string and return the new vector. This is the pipe-friendly form of stri_sub_all<-.

arguments.text: Arguments passed to stri_sub_all<-: str, from, to, length, omit_na, and use_matrix.

arguments.name: replacement
arguments.text: Replacement strings. A plain character vector is wrapped into a list. Used when value is omitted.

arguments.name: value
arguments.text: Replacement strings. When both are passed, value is written.

origin.details: The call is stri_sub_all<-. Ranges must be sorted and mutually disjoint. A negative length skips that piece. An empty replacement warns and yields NA. The all-replacement index rule differs from stri_sub_replace when from is not positive.
origin.value: A character vector of the replaced strings.
origin.example: stri_sub_replace_all("a b c", c(1, 3, 5), c(1, 3, 5), replacement = c("A", "B", "C"))

translation.description: Replace several substrings in each string and return the new strings. This calls stri_sub_all_assign.

arguments.name: args
arguments.text: Positional arguments of stri_sub_all_assign: str, from_, to, and length.

arguments.name: replacement
arguments.text: Replacement strings. A flat list is one character vector. A list of lists is one vector per string.

arguments.name: value
arguments.text: Replacement strings. When both are passed, value is written.

arguments.name: kwargs
arguments.text: omit_na and use_matrix, passed through to stri_sub_all_assign.

translation.details: The replacement is stri_sub_all<-, not stri_sub<-. Ranges must be sorted and disjoint. A negative length skips that piece. from_ = 0 with a positive length adds that length after rewriting from_ to 1.
translation.value: A list of the replaced strings.
translation.example:
from stringi.sub import stri_sub_replace_all
print(stri_sub_replace_all("a b c", [1, 3, 5], [1, 3, 5], replacement=["A", "B", "C"]))
